coverage: Sunday run. Nothing has traded since the Friday 7 Aug close — Friday's levels stand. What follows is what changed over the WEEKEND, which was not quiet.
tldr: THE WEEKEND CUT AGAINST FRIDAY'S TAPE: crude fell ~7% last week largely on Hormuz-reopening optimism, and over the weekend Tehran DISOWNED that premise — the IRGC called reopening "completely independent" of the Oman talks and the security council secretary said the strait "will never fully reopen" until Washington "corrects its behaviour".

LIVE ESCALATION: an IRGC missile struck an ADNOC tanker in the strait on Saturday — the 15th vessel hit since the conflict began. UAE called it piracy; Saudi, Qatar and the GCC condemned it. Vance offered no concession.
Expect oil to open firmer and last week's -7% to look over-discounted. That is a tailwind for your gold/silver miners after their 20%+ week, and a headwind for the dovish-inflation story.
OPERATIONAL: SGX is CLOSED Monday 10 Aug for National Day. Your entire Singapore sleeve — DBS, OCBC, the REITs, the developers — is untradeable, leaving ONE session (Tuesday) before Wednesday's CPI.

US July CPI lands Wednesday 12 Aug and is the decisive print for the September hike that collapsed to ~40-44% on Friday. TD Securities looks for core +0.20% m/m / 2.4% y/y — a house forecast made BEFORE the payrolls contraction.
Crypto gave no signal: BTC ~$64,904 and ETH ~$1,916, flat through the weekend — notable that it did not join the metals rally.

regime.label: Dovish repricing meets a re-arming oil risk
regime.oneLiner: Friday's dovish repricing stands, but the weekend re-armed the Hormuz risk that last week's crude slide had discounted away.

topNews.headline: IRGC missile hits ADNOC tanker in Strait of Hormuz — Gulf states condemn "act of piracy"
topNews.actionable: Crude closed Friday around Brent $83.55 / WTI $78.2 after a -7% week priced on de-escalation hopes. A live tanker strike on Saturday is the kind of event that can reverse part of that at Sunday-evening futures open. Watch the Brent open (Monday ~06:00 SGT) as the first tradeable read; also a potential safe-haven tailwind for the gold/silver sleeve, which does not price until Monday.

topNews.headline: Iran decouples Hormuz reopening from the Oman deal, hardens conditions on Washington
topNews.actionable: Oil fell ~7% last week and Brent sits ~$83 partly on reopening optimism. Saturday's messaging says the Oman deal does not reopen the strait — Iran is holding that as separate leverage over Washington. Treat Friday's crude weakness as having over-discounted a reopening, and expect a firmer Monday/Tuesday open in energy. The same hardening is supportive for the gold/silver miner complex after its 20%+ week.

topNews.headline: Iran attaches conditions: strait will not fully reopen until US "corrects its behaviour"
topNews.actionable: The gap between "framework finalized" and "strait stays shut until Washington concedes" is the whole trade. An Oman deal that does not actually restore transit traffic leaves the energy risk premium in place even as headlines read constructive. Watch tanker transit counts rather than deal headlines as the confirming signal.

topNews.headline: White House response: Vance says US is "really in the middle of the game," offers no concession
topNews.actionable: This is the answer to the White House question: no softening. With Iran demanding force withdrawal and sanctions relief and Washington signalling continued pressure, the gap between the two positions did not narrow this weekend. Keeps the Gulf risk premium intact into Monday.

topNews.headline: Iran-Oman lane framework near-final: northern inbound Iranian lane, southern Omani outbound, ~60-day interim
topNews.actionable: The mechanics are real progress but the framework is explicitly interim (~60 days) and unapproved, and per Saturday's IRGC comments does not itself reopen the strait. Any headline reading "Iran-Oman deal signed" should not be traded as a supply-normalisation event — check whether Tehran has also conceded on the US conditions before assuming crude downside.

topNews.headline: CALENDAR: SGX closed Monday 10 August for National Day — the entire Singapore book is untradeable
topNews.actionable: SG banks, REITs and developers do not trade Monday — no ability to react to the OCBC/DBS record-results follow-through or to any weekend Hormuz repricing until Tuesday 11 Aug. Anything Dom wants to do in the Singapore sleeve ahead of Wednesday's CPI must be queued for Tuesday, giving him one session rather than two.

signals: Oil is the live trade into Monday: Brent settled ~$83.55 pricing a reopening Tehran has now disowned, with a tanker struck on Saturday. Watch the Sunday-evening futures open as the first tradeable read.

Your miners (GDX +20% on the week) get a second tailwind if the Gulf premium re-arms — but that same premium is what could revive the inflation case and undo the dovish Fed repricing driving them. The two legs are not independent.

The levered silver position has run from ~$55.6 in late July to $63.54. With CPI Wednesday and Hormuz re-arming, this is a high-variance week for a 1.6x position — size is the decision, not direction.
SGX shut Monday compresses your Singapore decision window to Tuesday alone, right after record DBS and OCBC results and with the STI 15 points off its high.
BTC flat while gold and silver ripped is a divergence worth noting — the "debasement trade" is not moving together.
